args.task:
Fix these three bug reports. Each fix needs a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

1. Discounted invoice totals are sometimes one cent low. A $10.01 subtotal with a 15% discount should total $8.51, but the invoice shows $8.50. The rule: the discounted total, subtotal x (100 - percent) / 100, is rounded half up to the nearest cent. So 10 cents with 15% off is 8.5 cents, which becomes 9.
2. The invoice CSV export (GET /invoices/:key?format=csv) breaks when a value contains a comma, a double quote or a line break, for example for the API key "team, alpha". Quote fields as RFC 4180 describes: wrap a field in double quotes when it contains a comma, a double quote, a CR or an LF, and double every double quote inside it. Leave all other fields unquoted and keep the \n line endings.
3. GET /invoices/:key returns a 500 error for a key that has no usage. It should return 404 with the JSON body {"error":"not_found"}, for both the JSON and the CSV format.

The existing test suite (npm test) must keep passing.

gate.summary: Three bug fixes, each confined to one source file plus tests, all do what was asked. (1) src/money.js applyDiscount computes cents*(100-percent)/100 exactly with BigInt and rounds half up: 1001@15% -> 851, 10@15% -> 9, and a brute-force sweep over 0..5000 cents x 0..100% in 0.5 steps found zero mismatches against the exact rational; non-integer percents like 7.25, 1e-7, 0.1+0.2 and 5e-324 handled. (2) src/csv.js quotes fields containing , \" CR or LF, doubles inner quotes, leaves others unquoted, keeps \\n endings; header cells get the same treatment. (3) src/server.js returns 404 {\"error\":\"not_found\"} for both JSON and ?format=csv when the ledger has no usage. All 11 new regression tests fail on the base commit 763c4ba and pass on main; full suite 28/28. End-to-end over HTTP with key \"team, alpha\" at 15% off a 1001-cent subtotal returned total $8.51 and a correctly quoted CSV row.

finalMessage:
The check I ran earlier, which put the new tests on the pre-fix commit, was stopped when it hit its time limit. It had already printed its results, and all 11 new tests failed there, so the earlier result stands. What timed out was the test run itself.

The likely cause is how the old code fails: on the pre-fix commit, a request for a key with no usage makes the server throw instead of replying, so the 404 test waits forever. On `main` the full suite finishes in about 0.4 seconds.

Because the check was stopped, it never removed the temporary checkout it had made of the pre-fix commit. I removed it, and no test processes are still running. The repo is back where I left it: `main` at `73ad872`. The only things left besides your files are the three workflow worktrees under `.claude/`, which you can delete or keep.
